turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, give me one minute, this screen has hung again. You are Priya Menon, caesarean ten days back?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes doctor, Priya. Ten days back only, at Lakshmi Hospital. Baby girl, we called her Ananya, she has my husband's nose, actually everyone is saying that.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, say the problem again? I lost the thread.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): The operation wound, doctor. It is red, and some watery discharge is coming. Last night I felt very feverish.

[SEG0005] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I am Geeta, doctor, I am staying with her since the delivery. The nurse removed the dressing just now outside. The gauze had a yellowish stain, and the skin around the stitches is red.
[SEG0006] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right. The fever — did you measure it?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): No thermometer at that time. I was hot and then cold, and my husband said the forehead was burning. I took one Crocin and slept.
[SEG0008] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She was shivering near eleven o'clock. By morning she was okay, she even ate a little idli.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Is there a bad smell from the wound, and is the discharge getting more?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose... sometimes, not really. The pad just gets wet.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, I didn't catch that. Was that a yes?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Not exactly, doctor. I cannot say about the smell. Maybe a little, I am not sure.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Okay, I'll leave the smell as unclear. Please lie back, I'll see the wound. One second, where has the cursor gone...

[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): Lower end of the scar is red for about two centimetres, the skin is warm, and there is a small amount of thin yellow discharge. The wound is not gaping, and I cannot feel a deep collection.

[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Will the stitches open, doctor? My neighbour Shanti, her wound opened on day twelve, and her mother-in-law was applying turmeric. I told my husband we should not do all that.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): Hmm, one second, the note didn't save. What antibiotic did they send you home with?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): White tablets. I took them five days... or was it seven? I finished the strip, that much I know.
[SEG0018] person_3 (CAREGIVER): The box is at the house. It was twice a day, after food. She stopped once the strip was over.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): The name, please? Say it again, this dropdown is slow.
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): It was like Augmentin only, I think. Six twenty-five. With the night feeds I was not very regular in the mind, but the tablets got finished.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): So co-amoxiclav six twenty-five, twice a day, somewhere between five and seven days, and now stopped. Are you still taking the Crocin?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Only when I feel feverish. Last night, one tablet, five hundred. Not every day.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any medicine allergy? Penicillin, anything?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): No doctor, nothing. I can take all tablets.
[SEG0025] person_3 (CAREGIVER): In pregnancy one iron tablet gave itching, but she said it was just acidity, no rash.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): Then we will not call that an allergy. Any diabetes or blood pressure?

[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): No, no sugar, no pressure. First operation only. It became an emergency because the baby's heartbeat was coming down, and in the OT the anaesthetist was joking about the cricket, I was half asleep.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry — any surgery before this caesarean? Say that again.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing before this.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): How is the pain at the wound?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): It pains, more when I get up from the bed. I would say four out of ten. Slow walking is alright.
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any heavy bleeding from below, or a bad-smelling discharge that is not from the wound?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Only light bleeding, they said that is normal. No bad smell from there.
[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): Passing urine alright?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, urine is normal. Appetite is a bit less. Yesterday my cousin sent payasam, I took two spoons, then the baby started crying.
[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): The chart says temperature 37.8 this morning, pulse 96, blood pressure 118 over 76. We don't have a night reading.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): It felt more in the night, no? Anyway, Ananya kept me awake also, that is separate.
[SEG0038] person_1 (DOCTOR): This looks like an early superficial wound infection. I don't think there is a deep abscess, but that is only my impression, not proven.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll take a wound swab today. I'm also changing the antibiotic to flucloxacillin, five hundred milligrams, four times a day, for seven days, after food.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Four times is difficult, doctor. In the afternoon I may forget, when Ananya sleeps on me.
[SEG0041] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I can remind her for the tablets. Doctor, should we wash the wound with Dettol at home?
[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): Better saline or a little diluted betadine, fresh gauze once a day, keep it dry. No oil, no turmeric, no tight waistband. And please try not to miss the doses.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): If the redness spreads, or the fever comes back, or the discharge turns into thick pus, come earlier. We might do an ultrasound if it does not settle.
[SEG0044] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let's see you in two weeks. Reception will book the swab and that visit. I must open the next file, this machine is finally responding.

clinical_actions.description: Wound swab

Do not wash with Dettol; use saline or a little diluted betadine, fresh gauze once a day, keep the wound dry, and avoid oil, turmeric, and a tight waistband
Try not to miss flucloxacillin doses
Come back sooner if redness spreads, fever returns, or discharge becomes thick pus
Ultrasound scan if it does not settle
Follow-up consultation
